landing.eyebrow: Welcome to the heart of the kitchen
landing.headline: Shared grocery lists for people who share a fridge
landing.body: A small, friendly app for the everyday chaos of feeding a home — without the group chat spiral or the second bag of onions.
landing.ribbon: Built for households · Real-time sync · Free to use
landing.whoWeAreText: The Last Onion is a shared grocery list app for people who live together. Roommates, partners, families — anyone who shops from the same fridge and wants to stay on the same page.
landing.ourMissionText: Grocery shopping should feel like a shared chore chart, not a logistics puzzle. We built something calm, obvious, and a little bit whimsical — like a note on the fridge that syncs in real time.
landing.whatYouGetSub: Everything your kitchen table needs, nothing it doesn't.
landing.feature1Desc: Create lists for your home. Everyone in the household sees the same groceries — and what's already in the cart.
landing.feature2Desc: Check off milk on your phone while someone else adds bread. Changes show up instantly, no refresh needed.
landing.feature3Desc: Pin staples you always buy, or let the app learn your regulars. Add them to any list in one tap.
landing.feature4Desc: Items sort into vegetables, dairy, baking, and more. Edit categories to match how your kitchen actually works.
landing.ctaTitle: Start your first shared list today
landing.ctaBody: Create a household, invite the people you live with, and never wonder who's buying the onions again. Setup takes about a minute.

about.title: About The Last Onion
about.lead: A tiny app with a big job: keep everyone in your home on the same grocery page — without the drama.
about.ribbon: A note on the fridge, but it syncs in real time
about.shortVersionP1: The Last Onion is a shared grocery list for households. You make lists, add items, check things off, and everyone sees the updates right away. Categories keep vegetables separate from dairy. "Usual items" remembers the stuff you buy all the time.
about.shortVersionP2: That's pretty much it — on purpose.
about.whyWeMadeItP1: Shared shopping sounds simple until it isn't. Texts get buried. Paper lists vanish. Someone swears they told you about the milk.
about.whyWeMadeItP2: We wanted something calm and obvious — a single place where the whole household can see what's needed and what's already in the cart.
about.belief1Text: Re-add "carrots" and we reuse the same row — no duplicate lines cluttering your list.
about.belief2Text: Households, shared fridges, the people you actually cook with. Simple invites, no corporate nonsense.
about.belief3Text: No gamification, no streaks, no guilt. Just a list that stays in sync.
about.faq1A: Yep. Make lists, invite your household, shop together. No paywall for the basics.
about.faq2Q: Do I need to install anything?
about.faq2A: Nope — it works in your browser. You can add it to your home screen on your phone if you like.
about.faq3Q: What if someone isn't in my household?
about.faq3A: Invite them to a specific list instead. Handy for dinner parties or shared Costco runs.
about.faq4A: Because someone always buys a second bag of onions. We're trying to fix that.
